title: Fleet topology: one manager (the human's machine, which runs every singleton service) and stateless Linux workers. Local paths remain in roster overrides.

manager.description: The singleton manager: the human's machine that runs fleet-sync and hosts every singleton service (CLI proxy, Beszel hub).

id.description: A short stable id for the manager, used in reports.

tailscaleName.description: The manager's Tailscale MagicDNS name, without the trailing dot (tailscale status --json: .Self.DNSName).

neverSleepOnPower.description: Workers depend on the manager's singleton services, so it never sleeps on AC power.

schedule.description: How often the manager's scheduled jobs run. Each defaults to the interval in ansible/macos/policy.json.

syncMinutes.description: fleet-sync --schedule converges the fleet this often (default 30).

watchMinutes.description: fleet-watch checks the fleet and stores its heartbeat this often (default 15). Keep it well under the max-age-minutes of the heartbeat workflow.

id.description: A short stable id for the worker. A revision new to the fleet must pass on one worker, the canary, before the others receive it: the one named under canary, or else the first reachable worker in this order.

ssh.description: The worker's Host alias in the manager's ~/.ssh/config. It must work with BatchMode=yes and a host key already in known_hosts.

os.description: Workers are the Linux boxes: stateless, replaceable, never hosting a singleton service.

tailscaleName.description: The worker's Tailscale MagicDNS name, without the trailing dot.

user.description: The non-root worker account that can use sudo.

sshPort.description: The port sshd listens on, normally 22.

t3Port.description: The port the worker T3 server listens on, normally 3773.

toolProfiles.description: Tool profiles this worker installs on top of the fleet-wide ones: web (pnpm, Deno, Yarn), go, rust (with CMake and Ninja), jvm (Temurin). Each is a locked tool set dev-fleet ships.

exposure.description: What this worker opens beyond loopback and the tailnet. A field named here replaces the one of worker.exposure.

publicSsh.description: Break-glass: keep the SSH port open beyond the tailnet. Default false: after enrolment SSH is reached only over the tailnet.

publicPorts.description: Ports opened on every interface; a listener on one passes worker:exposure. Default none.

otherListeners.description: How worker:exposure reports a listener beyond loopback and the tailnet that no fleet service owns, such as an agent's development server on 0.0.0.0. The firewall closes it either way. Default warn; a fleet service there always fails.

canary.description: The id of the worker that proves a revision new to the fleet first. When it is unreachable, the next reachable worker proves it instead. Default: the first reachable worker.

services.description: Singleton services. Every one runs on the manager; workers are clients only.

endpoint.description: Public HTTPS origin of the CLI proxy every node uses.

accounts.description: How provider accounts signed in on the proxy are watched and chosen. See docs/accounts.md.

minimumUsable.description: proxy:account:<provider> warns when a provider has fewer usable accounts than this (default 2) and fails when it has none.

selection.description: Per provider (claude, codex, antigravity): which account an unpinned request goes to first. Accounts cooling down are always skipped.

order.description: Account labels (sign-in emails) first, in this order; the others follow in the order of their routing prefix.

managerAccount.description: Beszel account the manager enrolls nodes with.

viewerAccount.description: Read-only Beszel account visitors are signed in as.

backups.description: Scheduled off-machine backups of the monitoring hub. fleet-sync sets them through the hub's API, with the keys of the secrets monitoring-backup-access-key and monitoring-backup-secret-key; without this block the hub's backups are only read, and beszel:backup warns.

schedule.description: A cron expression in the hub's time zone, for example 0 3 * * *.

keep.description: How many scheduled backups the hub keeps.

storage.description: S3-compatible storage off the manager. Never its keys.

forcePathStyle.description: Path-style requests, for services that need them (MinIO).

architectures.description: Exactly the architectures the policy names for that release.

ubuntu.description: The worker release and its architectures, as the Ubuntu policy of the pinned dev-fleet names them.

requiredCapabilities.description: Readiness checks every worker must pass; normally all six.

githubLogin.description: The GitHub login every worker must be signed in as.

vaultUser.description: The Vault user each worker's own token is issued for.

toolProfiles.description: Tool profiles every worker installs on top of the base tools: web (pnpm, Deno, Yarn), go, rust (with CMake and Ninja), jvm (Temurin). Each worker passes a tool:<name> check for each of their tools.

tools.description: Single tools every worker installs: names of tools dev-fleet's mise.toml pins (for example fd or ripgrep). A tool it does not pin is refused; ask for it in an issue.

exposure.description: What every worker opens beyond loopback and the tailnet. Without it inbound traffic arrives only over loopback and the tailnet, sshd takes keys only and no root login, and published container ports are closed beyond the tailnet.

publicSsh.description: Break-glass: keep the SSH port open beyond the tailnet. Default false: after enrolment SSH is reached only over the tailnet.

publicPorts.description: Ports opened on every interface; a listener on one passes worker:exposure. Default none.

otherListeners.description: How worker:exposure reports a listener beyond loopback and the tailnet that no fleet service owns, such as an agent's development server on 0.0.0.0. The firewall closes it either way. Default warn; a fleet service there always fails.

worker.description: Policy every worker must meet. All but the two logins, the capabilities and the tools are fixed.

source.description: The Git repository machines take dev-fleet's code from: the one the package you run was published from, or your fork. Nodes only accept source from it.

ides.description: The IDEs every machine runs. Defaults to ["t3"]; the README's support matrix lists the supported ones.

t3.description: What every machine's T3 Code holds beyond the provider instances generated from the proxy's accounts.

profile.description: Top-level T3 settings every machine holds the same (tool servers, projects, selected preferences). Keys not named here stay local; a key edited on a machine since dev-fleet last wrote it is reported as a conflict, never overwritten.

requiredModels.description: Models T3 must offer, and the proxy must serve, for every account of a tool, by tool (claude, codex, opencode).

state.description: The bucket that holds the fleet state (the roster, the approved revision and the configuration last applied). Any S3-compatible service, or a directory. Never credentials: a devfleet command reads those from DEVFLEET_BUCKET_ACCESS_KEY_ID and DEVFLEET_BUCKET_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

endpoint.description: The https origin of the S3 service; omit for AWS S3.

prefix.description: Key prefix, so one bucket can hold several fleets. Default: dev-fleet.

directory.description: An absolute path on an attached disk or a mounted share.

secrets.description: Where this fleet keeps its secrets. env: DEVFLEET_SECRET_<NAME>; file: one file per secret; sops: one encrypted document; vault: a KV v2 location per secret.

monitoring-backup-access-key.description: Only with services.monitoring.backups: the access key of the hub's backup storage.

monitoring-backup-secret-key.description: Only with services.monitoring.backups: the secret key of the hub's backup storage.

notify-webhook-url.description: Only with the webhook notify target: the URL fleet-watch POSTs JSON to.

notify-ntfy-url.description: Only with the ntfy notify target: the ntfy topic URL fleet-watch publishes to.

tailnet-auth-key.description: Optional: a short-lived, single-use, tagged Tailscale auth key a new worker joins the tailnet with (fleet-node-seed).

locations.description: Required for every secret except github-token, which defaults to the field GITHUB_TOKEN beside proxy-client-key.

git.description: The Git identity every node, the manager included, commits with, and the GitHub credential helper it pushes with. fleet-sync writes them in ~/.config/git/config and measures them as worker:git-identity and worker:git-push-auth.

email.description: user.email of every commit, for example the account's noreply address.

verifyRepository.description: A GitHub repository the fleet's account can push to, ideally private. Each node lists it through git with its own credentials.

signing.description: Sign every commit and tag. ssh: each node makes an SSH key of its own (~/.ssh/dev-fleet-git-signing), which never leaves it, and signs with it; measured as worker:git-signing. GitHub shows the commits as verified once each node's public key is added as a signing key to the account.

notify.description: Where fleet-watch sends a notification when a machine becomes unhealthy or recovers. Each target's address is a secret: notify-webhook-url (a JSON POST) or notify-ntfy-url (an ntfy topic URL).

repeatHours.description: Notify again about a machine that stays unhealthy this often. 0 never repeats; the default is 24.

github.description: How every node signs in to GitHub. The fleet login is worker.githubLogin.

manager.description: fleet: the manager signs in as the fleet login. {login}: a person's own login, checked and never replaced.

credential.description: shared: one github-token for every node. per-node: github-token-<node> for each node.

scopes.description: Token scopes every node must have, such as repo and workflow.

repositories.description: owner/name of repositories every node must be able to push to.

organizations.description: Organisations whose single sign-on must have authorised the token.

sandbox.description: owner/name of a repository fleet-github-verify branches, pushes to and opens pull requests on, then cleans up.
